newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses regain poise after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses regain poise after Greenspan.

text.p: European investors regained some of their nerve on Friday, allowing share and bond markets to claw back some of Thursday's losses although interest rate worries continued to dominate.
U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan sparked Thursday's big selloff by hinting once more at an impending rise in U.S. interest rates.
Most European markets clawed back at least part of their losses during morning trade, but dealers warned of volatility with the expiry of index futures and options contracts in London and New York.
"We've held up fairly well so far, mainly thanks to the bond market," one London dealer said. "But everybody remains nervous and I would be surprised if we saw a lot of volume."

Share markets were helped in part by the dollar, which firmed against the mark and yen, building on Greenspan's remarks ahead of next Tuesday's meeting of the Fed's policy-setting open market committee.
A stronger dollar helps European exporters and was cited by Paris traders as one of the factors behind a 1.3 percent rebound in France's blue chip CAC-40 index.

It was a similar story in Frankfurt, where the DAX 30 index was up more than one percent in late floor trade. Rises at Europe's smaller bourses ranged from 2.05 percent in Amsterdam by 1225 GMT to 1.06 percent in Stockholm and 0.3 percent in Madrid.
The exception among major stock markets was London, where the FTSE 100 lurched either side of Thursday's depressed close.

The expiry of March index futures and options injected extra volatility into an already jittery cash market and the FTSE 100 index slipped back to a loss of 0.25 percent after briefly poking its nose into the plus column.

Dealers said the "triple-witching" expiry of U.S. stock options, index options and index futures could result in a torrid session on Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 57 points on Thursday.
"We have had an extremely volatile, twitchy session ahead of the expiry coming up," one dealer said. "The screens have been going blue, followed by red, followed by blue."

BAT Industries Plc was the main focus among individual stocks in London after a U.S. legal deal by Liggett Group Inc sent U.S. tobacco shares sharply lower. BAT shares clawed their way back from a 29 pence decline to stand six pence down at 483 by mid-session.
Traders said a recovery in bond markets on both sides of the Atlantic supported equities.
British and German government bond markets edged higher, tracking the overnight rebound in U.S. Treasuries, although the market remained nervous following Greenspan's comments.

"We're seeing a bit of a squeeze after T-bonds did a bit better overnight and with (German) Bunds doing so well," one senior British bond salesman said. "There is some money coming in to the market but I think most people really want to wait until next week," he said.
Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) also dominated the foreign exchange market, with Greenspan's comments adding to expectations of a quarter point rate rise .

Greenspan, who has repeatedly spooked the markets in recent months, acknowledged the current benign inflation outlook in the U.S. but highlighted the potential for inflationary pressures and reiterated the Fed's pre-emptive stance on monetary policy.

"The comments from Greenspan appear to greenlight a move higher on Tuesday," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London. "Greenspan had a clear way to dampen rate hike speculation and he didn't."
By 1225 GMT the dollar was trading at 1.6923 marks and 123.50 yen compared with 1.6916 marks and 123.74 yen in late European trade on Thursday.

"The dollar might not make much headway ahead of the FOMC but it's being buoyed by Greenspan's comments, which weren't as neutral as we expected," said Peter Wood, a currency trader at Bank of Boston in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1225 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.6923 marks and 123.50 yen compared with 1.6916 marks and 123.74 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1225 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 10.7 points, or 0.25 percent, at 4,247.4.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 34.1 points, or 1.34 percent, at 2,587.82.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 36.6 points, or 1.12 percent, at 3,301.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $351.70 against $352.00 on Thursday, while silver firmed three cents to $5.21.
